messages:
Priya: Quick post-launch note  we got a handful of signals overnight. Need a lightweight decision rule for what goes into a hotfix sprint vs vNext.

Tom: Agreed. Raw list from monitoring: 
- streaming latency regressions (p95 up 2.5x)
- chat truncation for sessions > 5k tokens
- embeddings similarity mismatch on small inputs
- minor dashboard telemetry gaps (missing labels)

Luis: I can take the embeddings ticket if we decide it's not a P0. Reproducer: running compare on 3 vectors gives drift vs baseline.

Priya: Proposal: compute an "impact score" = severity_weight * affected_customers + infra_risk_factor. If impact_score >= 20 -> immediate hotfix. Else -> schedule for next iteration with target milestone. Keeps decisions objective.

Tom: Example weights: severity_weight: P1=10, P2=5, P3=1. infra_risk_factor: node_restarts=10, perf_degrade=6. So streaming latency (P1, many customers) -> hotfix. Embeddings (P2, few customers) -> vNext.

Jules: Also add "customer SLA flag" - if paying customer with SLA complains, bump to hotfix queue regardless of score. FinOps asked for that yesterday.

Priya: Agree. Also we should limit hotfix scope to code-only, non-model changes for this week (no model re-rolls).

Tom: Rolling policy draft (json):
```
{"rollout_policy": {"canary_pct": 5, "stages": [10, 50, 100], "rollback_on_error_multiplier": 3}}
```
Keep CI gates: lint -> unit -> smoke -> canary-e2e.

ops-bot: Created incident card INC-3401 (post-launch perf spike).

Luis: I'll open PR for embeddings debug and add a small test harness to compare against baseline vectors.

Jules: For backlog grooming: recommend a fast groom session tomorrow to tag each issue with triage: [hotfix, vNext, backlog, docs]. Keep hotfix <= 3 tickets.

Priya: Action items: Tom will formalize weights and publish a scoring sheet; Jules schedules 30m groom; Luis starts PR; Priya will notify the top-5 affected customers with status + ETA.

ops-bot: Reminder: CI pipeline queued for branch/triage/2034.
